note: A large international multi-center cohort of 45 patients with ACBD6 deficiency did not identify pancytopenia or hematologic dysfunction as a core clinical manifestation, contrasting with an initial report in two siblings.

evidence.text: In a study of 45 affected individuals across 28 unrelated families, core manifestations were neurodevelopmental and progressive movement disorders; hematologic dysfunction or pancytopenia was not listed among recurring clinical cardinal features.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%)

evidence.text: Pancytopenia with severe infections was described as a previously unreported finding in two Thai siblings with an ACBD6 homozygous duplication.

source.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorder, Obesity, Pancytopenia, Diabetes Mellitus, Cirrhosis, and Renal Failure in ACBD6-Associated Syndrome: A Case Report
source.quote: Clinical manifestations that have never been previously reported include morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to deaths in their early 30s.
